intro.title: What does Exyconn build for logistics companies?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that take over the calls, messages and paperwork around each consignment: telling a customer where the truck is, proposing the day's routes, collecting POD photos from drivers, keeping e-way bills valid and warning the control room about loads that are running late. Exyconn designs, builds and runs them on your transport management system (TMS), warehouse system (WMS), GPS telematics and WhatsApp. Dispatchers and branch managers keep the decisions.

benefits.title: Why logistics firms are doing this now

items.text: Control rooms spend much of the day on tracking calls, when the GPS already has the answer.
Drivers and fleet owners already work on WhatsApp, so a bot can collect POD and updates without another app.
An e-way bill that expires mid-route, or a Part B not updated after a vehicle change, can hold goods at a checkpoint.
Detention at loading and unloading points eats margin that was already thin.
Customers pay against POD, so every missing or unreadable copy delays an invoice.

demo.title: whatsapp · consignment desk
demo.caption: A consignee asks about a delivery; the agent reads the GPS position and the e-way bill, and books an unloading slot.

messages.text: LR 48213, when will it reach our Chakan warehouse?
Hi Sandeep. The truck MH 12 XX 4417 is past Satara on NH48, about 150 km away. At its current speed it should reach Chakan around 3:30pm.
Our dock is busy until 4. Can it come at 4:30?
Yes. I've told the driver to report at 4:30 and booked dock slot 4:30–5:30 with your stores team. The e-way bill is valid until midnight, so there is no issue there.
Good. Send me the POD once unloaded
Will do. The driver will upload the signed copy here and I'll forward it to you and to billing.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a logistics team's hours actually go
props.lede: Spend a morning in any control room and the same work fills the day. It is routine, and it never stops.

items.title: Tracking calls on loop
items.text: Customers call for status, the coordinator calls the driver, then calls the customer back. The GPS portal had the location all along.

items.title: Dispatch planned on a whiteboard
items.text: Matching tonight's loads to available trucks and drivers happens on phone calls and memory, so part-loads and empty return legs go unnoticed.

items.title: POD that never arrives
items.text: Signed copies come back days later, crumpled or missing a stamp, and billing waits for them before the invoice can go out.

items.title: E-way bills nobody is watching
items.text: A transhipment or a breakdown means a Part B update, and a long delay means an extension inside a fixed window. Miss either and the load is at risk at the next check.

items.title: Bad news arriving last
items.text: A truck stuck at a checkpost or a consignment held at a hub is often discovered when the customer calls to complain.

items.title: Costs known after the month ends
items.text: Freight per lane, detention, fuel and on-time performance are assembled from several sheets, long after anything can be done about them.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your control room

items.title: Shipment tracking queries
items.text: Answers "where is my consignment" by LR, AWB or invoice number from GPS and TMS data, on WhatsApp, phone or a tracking page, and gives an ETA rather than a city name.

items.title: Route planning and dispatch
items.text: Proposes the day's load plan and routes from bookings, vehicle capacity and driver hours, and sends trip details to drivers once the dispatcher approves.

items.title: POD and e-way bills
items.text: Collects POD photos from drivers, checks for signature and stamp, attaches them to the trip in the TMS, and tracks each e-way bill's validity and Part B so your team updates or extends it in time.

items.title: Delay and exception alerts
items.text: Watches every trip against its plan and alerts the control room and the customer when a truck stops too long, leaves the route or will miss its slot.

items.title: Warehouse stock
items.text: Answers client questions on stock, inbound and outbound from the WMS, and flags slow-moving or near-expiry inventory to the warehouse manager.

items.title: Freight cost and on-time reports
items.text: Freight per lane, detention, empty kilometres and on-time delivery by customer and vendor, compiled daily from the TMS and sent to the managers who own them.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a 40-truck transport company
props.lede: Follow a weekday on the Mumbai–Pune–Bengaluru lanes. Each moment lights the part of the business the agent is working on.

moments.title: Today's plan, ready to approve
moments.text: Overnight bookings are matched to available trucks and drivers. The dispatcher reviews the proposed load plan, swaps one vehicle and approves it.

moments.title: Ten tracking calls that didn't happen
moments.text: Consignees ask about their loads on WhatsApp. Each gets the truck's position and an ETA from the GPS feed, with nobody in the control room picking up a phone.

moments.title: A breakdown caught early
moments.text: A truck has been stationary on the highway for 50 minutes. The control room is alerted, a replacement vehicle is arranged and the consignee is told the new ETA.

moments.title: Part B, updated in time
moments.text: The load moves to the replacement truck. The agent prompts the team to update the vehicle number on the e-way bill before it leaves, and confirms the update is done.

moments.title: A client asks about stock
moments.text: A client's planner asks how many cartons of one SKU are in the Bhiwandi warehouse. The agent answers from the WMS, including two inbound trucks expected tomorrow.

moments.title: The day's lanes in numbers
moments.text: On-time deliveries, detention hours, empty kilometres and freight per tonne by lane reach the owner, with the day's late trips listed by cause.

items.question: Will this replace our dispatchers and coordinators?
items.answer: No. It removes the routine tracking calls and document chasing. Load plans are proposals a dispatcher approves, and breakdowns, disputes and key-account issues go to your people with the trip history attached.

items.question: Which TMS and GPS systems can it connect to?
items.answer: Any TMS, ERP, WMS or GPS telematics provider that offers an API or a regular data export, including in-house systems. Where there is nothing to connect to, we start from your booking sheet and a GPS feed. We confirm what is possible in the first week.

items.question: Does the agent generate e-way bills by itself?
items.answer: It tracks validity and reminds your team to update Part B or extend a bill within the allowed window. Where your GST setup permits API access, it can prepare the update for a person to submit, and nothing is filed without your approval.

items.question: Can drivers use it in their own language?
items.answer: Yes. Drivers can send voice notes or messages in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and other Indian languages, and the agent replies in the same language. Most drivers only need to send a photo of the POD.

items.question: What about customer and driver data?
items.answer: Location, consignment and driver data stay in an environment set up for your company, with role-based access and an audit log. Location tracking is limited to trips, and the setup follows India's DPDP Act 2023, or the GDPR for European shipments.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on fleet size, trip volume and the systems we connect. Most firms start with the tracking desk at a fixed price for the first phase. Tell us about your operation and we'll quote it.
